shinychat

Source: vignettes/shinychat.Rmd
shinychat.Rmd

shinychat 0.5 and bslib 0.12 offcanvas pick up the same iOS 27 defaults as the rest of a glass app: refraction, morph, press, and the scroll edge. Pass theme = glass_theme() to page_chat(). An embedded chat_ui() inside any glass page uses the same CSS.

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(shinyglass)
library(shinychat)

ui <- page_chat(
  "Glass notes",
  id = "chat",
  theme = glass_theme(),
  placeholder = "Message",
  sidebar = chat_sidebar(history = TRUE, open = "always"),
  toolbar = toolbar(
    toolbar_input_button("open_sources", "Sources")
  )
)

The header, history sidebar, and drawer are glass chrome. User bubbles are tinted pills. The composer is a floating pill, like the iOS 27 Messages bar, and grows a fade when the transcript sits underneath it. Thinking rows, tool cards, citation chips (<shiny-aside>), attachment and text previews, toolbars, and the slash-command menu use the menu surface so they stay readable on the wallpaper.

offcanvas() panels use the same material. They still slide with Bootstrap’s transform. A separate scale grows the panel from the trigger when morph is on. Scrolling the panel body fades the header. Reduced motion skips that scale. Reduced transparency, increased contrast, and forced colors turn the lens off, as they do for other chrome.

observeEvent(input$open_sources, {
  show_offcanvas(offcanvas(
    id = "sources_panel",
    title = "Sources",
    placement = "end",
    "Citations stay in this panel."
  ))
})

Harbor notes is a core demo, with the dusk wallpaper behind the glass. The hosted app is Harbor notes. It answers with Gemini Flash and falls back to the local script if the API errors.

shiny::runApp(system.file("examples/shinychat-glass", package = "shinyglass"))

With no API key the reply is a local script. It streams a thinking panel, a short answer, a citation chip, and a tide-table tool card. GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY) switches that session to ellmer::chat_google_gemini() with Gemini Flash (gemini-3.7-flash, or SHINYGLASS_CHAT_MODEL). The system prompt helps with shinyglass, Shiny, R, and ordinary conversation, and declines only a clearly unrelated or abusive request. A small chip reads Live (Gemini) or Demo replies. A public session allows 8 messages of at most 400 characters. If the API errors or returns a quota response (429), a glass notice explains the fallback and the local script continues. The key is never written to the log or the page. The theme choice and the conversation are kept in the browser’s local storage, which is what “Notes stay on this machine” refers to. The shinychat history store stays in memory, so nothing is written to the server disk and no model is asked for a title. The sidebar starts open on desktop and collapses into the page menu on a phone.
